title: Ramayana Nears ₹1,700 Crore Worldwide, Passes Dhurandhar 2 in the US
excerpt: Day 18 added ₹35.60 crore net in India as the worldwide gross hit ₹1,693.50 crore — and its $28.4 million US total is now the highest ever for an Indian film.
body:
• Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana has reached ₹1,693.50 crore worldwide gross in 18 days, according to trade tracker Sacnilk — ₹1,126.50 crore gross (₹942.75 crore net) in India and ₹567 crore overseas.
  • Day 18, Sunday, November 22, brought ₹35.60 crore net in India, up 28.8 per cent from Day 17's ₹27.65 crore, across 16,277 shows at 37.9 per cent occupancy.
  • In the US, the film has reached $28.4 million, passing Dhurandhar: The Revenge's $28.1 million to set a new all-time US benchmark for an Indian film, per tracker Luiz Fernando.
  • Its Hindi net of ₹715.75 crore makes it the second-fastest film to ₹700 crore in Hindi net collections — 18 days, behind only Dhurandhar 2's 10 days. For diaspora viewers, the US record is the headline: no Indian film has earned more in America.

Eighteen days into its run, Ramayana is closing on ₹1,700 crore worldwide — and it has just taken a record that matters most to the diaspora audience. The Nitesh Tiwari directorial, headlined by Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Yash as Ravana with Sai Pallavi, stands at ₹1,693.50 crore worldwide gross, according to figures from trade tracker Sacnilk reported by The Hollywood Reporter India. In the United States, it has reached $28.4 million, moving past Dhurandhar: The Revenge's $28.1 million lifetime total to become the highest-grossing Indian film ever in the US market, per box office tracker Luiz Fernando.

"That closed the first three days of Week 3 at ₹79.00 crore net, after a Week 1 of ₹564.60 crore net (Days 1–8) and a Week 2 of ₹299.15 crore net (Days 9–15)."

The Day 18 numbers

The third Sunday delivered the weekend's expected jump. Day 18 (Sunday, November 22) collected ₹35.60 crore net in India, up 28.8 per cent from Day 17's ₹27.65 crore, across 16,277 shows at 37.9 per cent occupancy. That closed the first three days of Week 3 at ₹79.00 crore net, after a Week 1 of ₹564.60 crore net (Days 1–8) and a Week 2 of ₹299.15 crore net (Days 9–15). The film's India totals after 18 days: ₹942.75 crore net and ₹1,126.50 crore gross, with overseas contributing ₹567 crore — 33.5 per cent of the global gross.

Five languages, one ledger

Ramayana was released in Hindi, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam and Tamil versions, and the language split shows a Hindi-led but genuinely pan-India run: Hindi accounts for ₹715.75 crore of the India net, followed by Kannada at ₹75.30 crore, Telugu at ₹56.60 crore, Malayalam at ₹48.45 crore and Tamil at ₹46.65 crore, across 3,96,864 shows in India. The Hindi figure carries its own milestone — at 18 days, Ramayana is the second-fastest film to ₹700 crore in Hindi net collections, behind Dhurandhar 2 (10 days) and ahead of Pushpa 2 (20 days) and the original Dhurandhar (25 days).

The global chart, and what is left to chase

Globally, tracker Nishit Shaw placed the film at #3 on Rentrak's global chart for the weekend with an estimated $182.9 million over 18 days, while Fernando put its global tally at $183 million across 48 markets — a figure that moves it past RRR's $166.6 million global run on the all-time Indian list. The one overseas crown it has not taken is the lifetime one: Aamir Khan's Dangal remains the highest-grossing Indian film overseas at $233.8 million, a total built on its historic Phase 2 runs in China.

The remaining targets are now a short list of the biggest Indian films ever made. Ahead of Ramayana's ₹1,693.50 crore stand Pushpa 2: The Rule (₹1,742 crore), Baahubali 2: The Conclusion (₹1,788 crore) and Dhurandhar: The Revenge (₹1,813 crore). Whether it catches them depends on how the weekdays of Week 3 hold after a third weekend that finished well below the second — the trajectory Sacnilk's own tracking flagged even as the Sunday number jumped. For US audiences, though, the argument is already settled: the biggest Indian film in American box office history is a Hindi-language mythological epic, three weekends into its run.
